_readme: Namespaces this project has retired: swept to zero occurrences in extractions/ by
normalise-ids.py, and refused by gate-evidence.py from then on, whatever a record's
A prefix belongs here only once the sweep is COMPLETE - verified by counting the
prefix in extractions/ and getting nought. That is what licenses ignoring
registry_status: `extraction-layer` means 'reused from an earlier extraction record',
and for a retired prefix there is no earlier record left to have reused, so the
declaration cannot be true. It is also the difference between this rule and
check_id_hygiene's two, which fire on `minted` only because the corpus still contains
the ids they describe and re-extraction has to be able to reuse them.
`cloud-providers:` is deliberately NOT here. Its sweep is incomplete on purpose:
cloud-providers:gcp-azure is one id standing for two promoted providers, minted
because one sentence gave both the same rule, and rewriting it to either would
silently drop the other. A prefix with one live id is not retired.
`use_instead` is prose because a retired prefix has no single destination - that is
usually why it was retired. Round 15's rule: a dissolution's destination is not a

indexes:.use_instead: `index-type:` for a KIND of index (primary, secondary, composite-secondary, functional, array, partial, named-primary, gsi, hyperscale-vector, composite-vector, search-vector, analytics-index, view); `index:` for anything else true of indexes - settings, storage modes, rebalance methods, pushdowns, scan mechanics, on-disk artifacts; `storage-engine:` for an engine (plasma, forestdb, nitro, couchstore, magma); `vector-search:` for a vector-index artifact or tuning parameter; `page:` if what you are naming is a document rather than a thing. This prefix existed only because Capella files these pages in a directory called `indexes/`, and an id names its subject, not the directory the page was in.

vector-index:.use_instead: `vector-search:` for the subject area (settings, metrics, artifacts), `index-type:` for the three vector index types, `vector-similarity-metric:` for the four-member metric enum, `n1ql:` for the two SQL++ distance functions. The prefix was named like an axis and populated like a subject area.

setting:.use_instead: whatever owns the setting - `n1ql:` for a Query service setting or request parameter, `index:` for an Index service setting, `data:` for a Data service one, `tls:` for encryption configuration. A setting is always a setting OF something, so this prefix could only ever hold other namespaces' business.

setting-scope:.use_instead: `n1ql:request-level-query-parameters`, `n1ql:node-level-query-settings`, `n1ql:cluster-level-query-settings`. This one WAS a real closed axis - three members, no fourth - and was still folded, because it was a third spelling of three concepts round 10 had already promoted from the same page. If a later round finds cluster-versus-node scoping evidenced outside the Query service, mint it again then, with the citation.

tools:.use_instead: `tool:` - a plain singular/plural fork, and the cheapest kind of defect to prevent. check_id_hygiene's rule 1 now blocks minting a new one.
